### sqs-consumers-keep-idempotency-tokens-ignore-duplicates

**Claim.** A message that was published once may be delivered more than once. A publisher can include idempotency tokens, and consumers should keep track of each token received and ignore messages with duplicate tokens.

**Write it as.** `may be accidentally delivered more than once` · `keep track of each token received`

**Scope.** event-driven architectures with message queues.

> "In some circumstances, a message that was published only once may be accidentally delivered more than once. When a publisher generates and includes idempotency tokens in messages, it requests that the processing of any duplicate message received doesn't result in a repeated action for the same message. Consumers should keep track of each token received and ignore messages that contain duplicate tokens."
> — [REL04-BP04 Make mutating operations idempotent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/reliability-pillar/rel_prevent_interaction_failure_idempotent.html)

### sqs-copies-on-multiple-servers-cause-duplicates

**Claim.** SQS stores copies of a message on multiple servers. If a server that holds a copy is unavailable when you receive or delete a message, the copy is not deleted there and you might get that message copy again, so applications must be idempotent.

**Write it as.** `isn't deleted on the server that is unavailable` · `you might get that message copy again` · `Design your applications to be idempotent`

**Scope.** SQS standard queue; a server holding a copy is unavailable at receive or delete time.

> "Amazon SQS stores copies of your messages on multiple servers for redundancy and high availability. On rare occasions, one of the servers that stores a copy of a message might be unavailable when you receive or delete a message."
> — [Amazon SQS at-least-once delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues-at-least-once-delivery.html)

> "If this occurs, the copy of the message isn't deleted on the server that is unavailable, and you might get that message copy again when you receive messages. Design your applications to be idempotent (they should not be affected adversely when processing the same message more than once)."
> — [Amazon SQS at-least-once delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues-at-least-once-delivery.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### sqs-metric-age-of-oldest-message-measures-lag

**Claim.** The ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric reports, in seconds, the age of the oldest unprocessed message in the queue. It is reported if the queue contains at least one active message.

**Write it as.** `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` · `oldest unprocessed message in the queue`

**Scope.** SQS queue CloudWatch metric.

> "ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage | The age of the oldest unprocessed message in the queue. | Seconds | Reported if the queue contains at least one active message. | + For standard queues, if a message is received three or more times and not deleted, SQS moves it to the back of the queue. The metric then reflects the age of the next message that hasn’t exceeded the receive threshold. This reordering occurs even when a redrive policy is in place. <br />+ Poison-pill messages (those repeatedly received but never deleted) are excluded from this metric until successfully processed. <br />+ When a message is moved to a DLQ after exceeding the `maxReceiveCount`, the age resets. In that case, the DLQ’s metric reflects the time the message was moved—not when it was originally sent. <br />+ FIFO queues don't reorder messages to preserve order. A failed message blocks its message group until it's deleted or expires. If a DLQ is configured, the message is sent there after the receive threshold is met." (columns: Metric | Description | Units | Reporting behavior | Key notes)
> — [Available CloudWatch metrics for Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-available-cloudwatch-metrics.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-14.

### sqs-metric-not-visible-messages-is-in-flight

**Claim.** The ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible metric counts in-flight messages: messages that were received but not yet deleted or expired. Use it to track processing delays or stuck consumers.

**Write it as.** `ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible` · `received but not yet deleted or expired`

**Scope.** SQS queue CloudWatch metric.

> "ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible | The number of in-flight messages that have been received but not yet deleted or expired. | Count | Reported if in-flight messages exist. | + Messages enter the in-flight state after being sent to a consumer via the `ReceiveMessage` API. <br />+ These messages are temporarily hidden from other consumers during the visibility timeout window. <br />+ Use this metric to track message processing delays or stuck consumers. <br />+ On rare occasions, one of the servers that Amazon SQS uses to store your messages might be unavailable when Amazon SQS reports queue metrics. When this occurs, this metric might report a non-zero value, including when the queue is otherwise empty or has had no `ReceiveMessage` calls. It typically resolves within minutes, so if you set an alarm for this metric, evaluate multiple consecutive data points rather than a single non-zero value." (columns: Metric | Description | Units | Reporting behavior | Key notes)
> — [Available CloudWatch metrics for Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-available-cloudwatch-metrics.html)
